newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Princess Anne visits British troops, school.
newsitem.headline: Princess Anne visits British troops, school.

text.p: Britain's Princess Anne on Wednesday visited the northern part of Bosnia under Serb control to talk to British troops serving in the NATO-led peace force and tour a school they built.
Queen Elizabeth's only daughter meet the Sherwood Foresters in the British military base in the town of Krupa na Vrbasu, 30 km (18 miles) south of Banja Luka.
Later in the morning she visited the Vojislav Ilic elementary school in Krupa na Uni.
The school was reconstructed after the bitter 43-month old war war by British soldiers and funded by the British Overseas Development Agency (ODA).

School director Djuka Vukovic thanked the princess for the visit and the British troops and government for what they had done for the shcool. "This is the most important date in the five-year history of the school," he said.
Princess Anne later left for Mrkonjic Grad and Sipovo to visit British troops from the Royal Logistics Corps.
She is due to return to the British military base, centre of the IFOR multinational division, in Ranici, some 10 km (six miles) from Banja Luka later in the day.

The princess arrived in Sarajevo on Tuesday to visit some of the 12,000 British soldiers enforcing the Dayton peace accords in the former Yugoslav republic and talk to Moslem and Croat members of Bosnia's newly-elected collective presidency.
The British embassy in Sarajevo said the meeting was purely a "courtesy visit".
Serb members of the presidency refused to attend an inaugural ceremony last Saturday in Sarajevo's national theatre, alleging the venue was unsafe for Serb leaders.
Bosnian Serb forces laid siege to Sarajevo and shelled the city throughout the 3-1/2 year conflict.
